newsitem.title: USA: EDS says quarterly sales to keep vacillating.
newsitem.headline: EDS says quarterly sales to keep vacillating.

text.p: Electronic Data Systems Corp's chief financial officer said quarterly sales will continue to vacillate from strong to weak and the company expects to continue to have some weak quarters.

"Sales are very lumpy. We cannot predict when we are going to close a deal," CFO Jody Grant told a Robertson, Stephens & Co conference. "We have had weak quarters and we will continue to have weak quarters," because fluctuation is the nature of the business, he said.
Grant told the group that Wall Street analysts' mean estimate of its 1997 earnings is $2.40 a share.

Grant said EDS is implementing a strategy to smooth the lumpiness of its businesses, particularly the margins it achieves from new contracts. He explained that EDS will pursue both high margin, higher risk business and low margin, lower risk business with a goal of an overall even margin.
The goal is "a portfolio profile that produces target operating margins," he said with the target of maintaining "historical" margin levels, he said.
EDS recently changed its business relationship with its former owner, General Motors Corp.

One side effect of the changed relationship has been lower margins at EDS in recent quarters. Grant explained the change, and described it as temporary but did not say exactly when the margin is expected to improve again.

Grant called market opportunity for EDS in 1997 "extremely robust," and added that EDS expects the overall market to grow 7.5 percent on a compounded annual rate between now and 2002. Pockets of the market are growing at 20 percent, however, he said.
